;Disasters and accidents
*[[2018 UY Aviation King Air C90 crash]] 
**A light aircraft crashes in the [[Ghatkopar]] district of [[Mumbai]], India, killing all four occupants and one person on the ground. [https://www.ndtv.com/mumbai-news/chartered-plane-crashes-in-mumbai-fire-engines-rush-to-spot-1874631 (NDTV)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-44641927 (BBC)]
*A fire breaks out at the Gikomba market in [[Nairobi]], Kenya, with 15 people confirmed dead and many homes and stalls being destroyed. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-44640504 (BBC)]
*A [[landslide]] killed 14 people in northern [[Myanmar]]. [https://www.bnionline.net/en/news/fourteen-people-killed-hpakant-after-heavy-rain-triggered-landslides (BNI Multimedia Group)]

;International relations
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**A summit meeting between [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] and [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] is set for July 16 in [[Helsinki]]. The leaders are expected to discuss national security issues as well as [[Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections|Russian interference in the 2016 U.S. elections]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-putin-summit-helsinki-finland-july-16/ (CBS News)]

;Law and crime
*[[Capital Gazette shooting]]
**A shooting at the office of ''[[The Capital]]'' and the ''[[Maryland Gazette]]'' newspapers in [[Annapolis]], [[Maryland]], United States, kills five people. The suspected shooter is detained by local police. [http://www.cbc.ca/news/world/capital-newspaper-shooting-annapolis-1.4726933 (CBC)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-44645986 (BBC)]
*[[Protests against Trump administration family separation policy]]
**About 575 women are arrested during a sit-in at the [[Hart Senate Office Building]] protesting the [[Trump administration family separation policy]]. [https://www.npr.org/2018/06/28/624401005/hundreds-arrested-protesting-trump-administrations-immigration-policies (NPR)]
**Police arrest at least nine protesters at an [[Occupy ICE]] demonstration in [[Portland, Oregon]]. [https://www.oregonlive.com/portland/index.ssf/2018/06/authorities_move_to_reopen_ice.html (''The Oregonian'')]
*[[2017-18 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**The [[Audiencia Nacional (Spain)|National Court]] confirms the prosecution against Major of the [[Mossos d'Esquadra]], [[Josep Lluís Trapero Álvarez|Josep Lluís Trapero]] and the former leaders of the regional Police for sedition and criminal organitzation. [http://www.elmundo.es/espana/2018/06/28/5b34dd7a46163f81658b45b3.html (''El Mundo'')]

;Politics and elections
*Aftermath of [[first impeachment process against Pedro Pablo Kuczynski]]
**The Prosecutor's Office of [[Peru]] opens a preliminary investigation to determine if there were alleged political benefits – among them [[Pardon of Alberto Fujimori|the humanitarian pardon]] granted to former [[President of Peru|President]] [[Alberto Fujimori]] – offered by former President [[Pedro Pablo Kuczynski]] to avoid being removed from his office during the first impeachment process against him in December 2017. Three months later, in the middle of a similar scenario, Kuczynski resigned, seeing that Congress would no longer favor him. <!-- needs to be shortened --> [https://peru21.pe/politica/fiscalia-investiga-ppk-ofrecio-beneficios-evitar-vacancia-411948 (Perú 21)]

;Sports
*[[2018 FIFA World Cup]] 
**[[Japan national football team|Japan]] is the only [[Asian Football Confederation|Asian]] team to advance to the [[2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage|knockout stage]], via fair play after exhausting other tiebreakers. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44439298 (BBC)]
